library_preparation_preflight.summary: ojdbc8's POM declares zero dependencies, so the generated scaffold test would only exercise basic driver registration. The near-identical sibling ojdbc11 (same vendor, same driver internals, same dependency-free POM shape) required four extra test-scope Maven dependencies plus a system property to reach its optional code paths (XML DB, PKI wallet auth, connection pooling, JSON/OSON, observability) without a live database. All four coordinates publish at ojdbc8's exact version (23.26.1.0.0), so the same setup applies here.

deterministic_setup.reason: Universal Connection Pool classes are optionally referenced by the thin driver's internals; without ucp on the classpath those pooling code paths are never loaded during agent tracing.
PKI/wallet-based authentication (SEPS, SSL wallet) is an optional driver integration only reachable when oraclepki is present.
XML DB type support (XMLType, OPAQUE/ADT mapping) is optional and only loaded when xdb is on the classpath.
Paired with xdb for XML DB type marshalling used by the driver's optional XML code paths.
Oracle's Dynamic Monitoring Service classes back the driver's optional observability/diagnostics instrumentation.
Backs the driver's optional OSON/JSON type support code paths.
Assertion library used throughout the sibling ojdbc11 test suite for readable multi-field assertions; reuse for consistency if tests are written in that style.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Set the system property oracle.jdbc.diagnostic.enableObservability=true for both the JVM test task and the native test run (add -Doracle.jdbc.diagnostic.enableObservability=true to nativeTest runtimeArgs) so the driver's DMS-backed observability code paths are exercised, matching the ojdbc11 precedent. No live Oracle Database or Docker image is required — ojdbc11's coverage is achieved entirely through unit-style tests against driver-internal classes (connection wrappers, type converters, proxy factories, auth services) without an actual database connection, so ojdbc8 should follow the same pattern rather than introducing a Docker-based Oracle DB image.
risks: ojdbc8 targets JDK 8/11 compatibility and may lack some newer JDBC 4.3 features present in ojdbc11 (which targets JDBC 4.3) — verify during generation which of ojdbc11's optional integrations (e.g., OSON, sharding, transaction replay) actually exist in ojdbc8's internals before assuming full parity.
The dms coordinate/version is independent of the driver's own version scheme; confirm 11.2.0.4 is still the version compatible with the 23.x driver line at generation time.
